title: The Nazca Lines Mystery
hook: In 1940, pilots first saw giant desert drawings in Peru that still puzzle researchers.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: In 1940, Peruvian pilot Juan Pablo Cueva spotted giant lines from the sky over Nazca.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: The geoglyphs include a hummingbird, a spider and a 370-meter long monkey, dated to 500 BC.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Researchers using satellite imagery in 2015 confirmed over 300 figures, some only visible from high altitude.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: Archaeologists link the lines to the Paracas culture, using stone removal to expose lighter soil.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: One theory proposes the figures served as astronomical markers aligned with solstice sunrise.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: Recent 2022 lidar scans revealed hidden lines beneath the surface, suggesting the site is far more extensive than previously thought.

end.line: What purpose could these massive desert drawings truly serve?

description: Exploring the mysterious Nazca Lines and the clues that keep researchers guessing.

facts.claim: In 1940, Peruvian pilot Juan Pablo Cueva first reported the Nazca Lines from the air
The Nazca geoglyphs include a hummingbird, spider and a 370-meter long monkey dating to around 500 BC
Satellite imagery in 2015 confirmed over 300 geoglyphs, many only visible from high altitude
Archaeologists associate the lines with the Paracas culture (c. 800-100 BC) using stone removal technique
Lidar surveys in 2022 uncovered previously unknown lines beneath the surface
